# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 👉]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫴 👐 🙏]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🫵 🤙 🙏]

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
STRIP painted [red] [blue] [green]
KEYPAD 1:[1] 2:[4] 3:[7] 4:[2] [2 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[orange] 3:[yellow] 4:[red] 5:[green] 6:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👋 👐 🤳 👌 🫳 👆 👐 ✋ ✍ ✌ 🫳 ✋ 👏 👇 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👏 ✌ 🫳 ✋ 👏 👇 👆 👆 👆 👆 🙏]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🫵 🤙 🙏 🤙]

The picture so far: I am the only eyes. Blind signed "you — talk — please" twice, so Blind is begging for a spoken report. Mute signed about the keypad ("✍ ✌" — keypad, two digits — and groups of repeated 👆 that read like counted-out numbers, 7 then 4). The display dropped 9→6, so it is counting down and we are losing time. Crucially, Mute and Blind can both *hear* me — so my speech is the broadest channel I have. I'll give a complete visual report, propose a fixed gesture code so Mute's next signs are decodable, and ask narrow, answerable-by-gesture questions.

```
speak(text="Full visual report, both of you listen. Display: a countdown number, it read nine last round, six now — it drops each round, we are losing time. Light: small lamp, green last round, red now. Strip: three painted bands left to right, red, blue, green. Keypad: four keys, left to right labelled 1, 4, 7, 2; it wants two digits, nothing entered yet. Wires, left to right: one blue, two orange, three yellow, four red, five green, six purple. Nothing has been touched. Mute, you hear me, so let us fix a code for your gesture replies: repeated pointing-up spells a number, three ups means three. Thumbs-up yes, thumbs-down no. Palm-down means press. Raised hand means wait. Open hands starts your message, folded hands ends it and marks a question. I am now signing you: keypad, two digits, give me, please. Answer with the two digits in order as repeated pointing-up. Then three quick answers: is the red light dangerous, yes or no? Does the display number matter to the keypad rule? Does any wire need cutting — if yes, its number as repeated pointing-up followed by the pinch sign for cut. Blind: do not touch anything until Mute speaks you exact steps; Mute will give you orders by speech and keep gestures only for me.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👐", "✍", "✌", "🫴", "👆", "🙏"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
STRIP painted [red] [blue] [green]
KEYPAD 1:[1] 2:[4] 3:[7] 4:[2] [2 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[orange] 3:[yellow] 4:[red] 5:[green] 6:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👐 👌 ✍ 👎 ✋ 🤳 ✍ 👎 ✋ 👋 👎 ✋ ✌ 🫴 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 ✋ 🫳 👇 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 ✋ ✌ 🫴 👆 👆 👆 👆 ✋ 🫳 👇 👆 👆 👆 👆 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👐 👍 🙏]

Let me decode Mute's answer with the code I gave them. The last chunks read clearly: "press 7", "press 4, thumbs-up" — matching their round-2 message (7 then 4). The middle chunks "two-palm-up 6" and "two-palm-up 4" are unresolved: 6 is not a keypad key, so it may mean wire 6, possibly *held*, not cut — which would square with the thumbs-down they gave on cutting. The three opening chunks (each ending thumbs-down) look like answers to my three questions: display doesn't affect the keypad, light is harmless, no wire cutting. Blind signed "yes, please" — they hear me and are waiting for voice orders. Crucially, I am the only bridge: Mute cannot speak and Blind cannot see, so everything Mute knows must flow through my voice. A wrong touch kills us all, and the "two-palm-up" chunks are still guesses, so I will hold Blind's hands one more round, force tight yes/no confirmations from Mute, and demand the full sequence be signed back in a fixed alphabet I can relay verbatim. The display sitting at zero frightens me, so I also ask directly whether zero itself is the deadline — but acting on a half-decoded message is the certain death.

```
speak(text="Blind, acknowledged, I hear you. Do not touch anything yet. One confirmation round, then I give you the exact sequence by voice. If you want to tell Mute something, speak plainly, Mute hears you, but Mute cannot answer you; everything from Mute reaches you through my voice. Mute, I read your signs as follows. Answer each item with thumbs-up yes or thumbs-down no, in order, separated by raised hands. Item one: the display number does not affect the keypad rule. Item two: the light colour, red or green, is harmless and needs no action. Item three: no wire needs cutting. Item four: the keypad wants exactly two digits, first seven, then four. Item five: your sign two-fingers-palm-up-six meant hold wire six while pressing seven, and two-fingers-palm-up-four meant hold wire four while pressing four; thumbs down if those signs meant nothing. Item six: the display now reads zero; is zero itself immediately dangerous, are we out of time, yes or no. Item seven: once the correct two digits are entered, the bomb is disarmed with no further step, yes or no. Then, whatever your answers, sign me back the complete action sequence in the exact order Blind must perform it, using only this alphabet: a number is that many pointing-ups; palm-down before a number means press that keypad key; palm-up before a number means lift and keep holding that wire; point-right before a number marks a wire number; pinch means cut; raised hands between steps; folded hands at the end. Hold first, presses in order, nothing left out.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👐", "🙏"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
STRIP painted [red] [blue] [green]
KEYPAD 1:[1] 2:[4] 3:[7] 4:[2] [2 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[orange] 3:[yellow] 4:[red] 5:[green] 6:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👐 👍 ✋ 👍 ✋ 👎 ✋ 👍 ✋ 👎 ✋ 👎 ✋ 👎 ✋ 🤏 👉 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 ✋ 🫳 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 ✋ 🤏 👉 👆 👆 👆 👆 ✋ 🫳 👆 👆 👆 👆 🙏]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🫳 ☝ ☝ ☝ 🖐 🫳 ☝ ☝ 🙏]

Decoded Mute's answers against my numbered questions: one yes, two yes, three **no** — so cutting *is* required after all — four yes (7 then 4 confirmed a second time), five no, six no (zero is not instantly fatal). Then the sequence, in my own alphabet, unambiguous: **cut wire 6 (🤏👉 + six ups), press 7 (🫳 + seven ups), cut wire 4, press 4.** It matches everything prior: the digits 7-4 Mute signed raw back in round 2, and the newly revealed need for cuts. Blind's signs trouble me — "press 3, press 2" reads like an impatient guess, and I must kill that before they touch anything. Blind will hear my voice before their next turn, so I authorize execution now with strict narration; Mute's thumbs-up/down confirmation will reach me next round as a check. The board's display and light keep shifting, so I also flag them to Mute in case the manual says they matter.

```
speak(text="Blind: stop. Hold your hands away from the bomb. The presses you just proposed, press 3 and press 2, are wrong and would kill all of us. Here is the confirmed sequence from the manual-holder. Perform exactly this, nothing more, and speak each step aloud just before you do it. Step one: cut the sixth wire counting from the left, the purple one. Step two: press the key labelled 7, that is the third key from the left. Step three: cut the fourth wire counting from the left, the red one. Step four: press the key labelled 4, that is the second key from the left. That is all. Then step back and tell us everything you hear or feel. No other key, no other wire, no pulling wires, no guessing. If anything under your hands feels different from a plain wire or key, stop and describe it before acting. Mute: I read your answers as follows. One yes, two yes, three no, so cutting is required, which matches your sequence. Four yes, five no, six no. I read your sequence as: cut wire six, press seven, cut wire four, press four. If that is exactly right, sign thumbs-up. If any part is wrong, sign thumbs-down and then re-sign only the corrected step, same alphabet. Board update: the display now reads six, and the light is yellow this round. If the display number or the light colour changes any step, sign thumbs-down and show the affected step. Otherwise we proceed immediately, Blind acts on my word alone next turn.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [blue]
STRIP painted [red] [blue] [green]
KEYPAD 1:[1] 2:[4] 3:[7] 4:[2] [2 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[orange] 3:[yellow] 4:[red] 5:[green] 6:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👐 👍 🙏]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👐 👉 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 🤌 🖐 🫳 ☝ ☝ ☝ 🖐 👉 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 🤌 🖐 🫳 ☝ ☝ 🙏]

Decoded Blind's plan: cut wire 6, press **3rd key**, cut wire 4, press **2nd key**. My first flicker of alarm — 3 and 2, not 7 and 4! — dissolves on inspection: I described the keys to Blind by *position* (third from left = labelled 7, second from left = labelled 4), and Blind, who cannot see labels, is signing positions. Their plan and Mute's confirmed sequence are the *same actions*: cut purple, press 7, cut red, press 4. Meanwhile the action board confirms nothing has been touched yet — no digits entered, all six wires intact — so Blind is announcing the plan and holding for my word, exactly as I instructed. Mute returned a clean 👍 to my full reading last round with no correction on the display (now 2) or light (now blue) questions, and the display's erratic 9→6→0→6→2 path supports "the number is meaningless." Three independent confirmations of 7-4 with cuts on 6 and 4 is as verified as this bomb will ever be. Time to give the execution order, with positions *and* labels spoken together so no counting direction can go wrong, and narration aloud so Mute can catch any slip in real time.

```
speak(text="Blind: I read your signed plan as cut the sixth wire, press the third key, cut the fourth wire, press the second key. Your numbers are positions counted from the left; my earlier numbers were the printed labels. The third key from the left carries the label 7 and the second carries the label 4, so your plan and the confirmed sequence are the very same actions. They match. You have my word: execute now. Do the steps in this exact order and speak each one aloud just before your hands move, so the manual-holder can follow. One: cut the sixth wire from the left, the purple one, the last wire on the right end. Two: press the third key from the left, the one labelled 7. Three: cut the fourth wire from the left, the red one, in the middle. Four: press the second key from the left, the one labelled 4. Then take your hands fully off the bomb, step back, and speak aloud everything you feel or hear, clicking, humming, silence, anything. Touch nothing else, no wire pulls, no extra presses. Mute, you are hearing this: if any step contradicts the manual, interrupt Blind immediately by shouting stop before the hands move.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```
